reason_codes.description: Nostr event id or BIP-340 signature verification failed.
Missing or non-byte-equal raw NIP-01 input.
An Assurance event content object or required addressable-event binding is not in its exact registered closed profile.
Cold-root inception and active-key acceptance do not reciprocally bind the same exact active key, inception event, and cold-root signature.
An Assurance record predecessor does not equal the event ID required by the accepted chain or associated-key state.
An Assurance acceptance, succession, or associated-key record binds a head other than the verifier's accepted head.
The current Assurance policy does not authorize the presented succession, recovery, epoch, associated-key issuer, or downgrade proof.
Distinct valid witness receipts do not reach the threshold fixed by the predecessor Assurance state.
Competing individually authorized successors of one accepted Assurance head cannot be uniquely selected.
The proposed successor key did not prove acceptance of the exact authorized succession claim.
Assurance authority is requested for material at or after the accepted compromise cutoff.
A compromise succession carries a subordinate reauthorization or a consumer attempts an implicit subordinate continuation.
An active public-agent grant omits the subject key's required proof of possession and consent; issuer-authorized revocation never requires subject cooperation.
An associated-key subject proof does not verify over the exact registered Assurance binding.
Verifier time is at or after an associated key's optional exclusive expiry bound.
The selected head-bound associated-key state is revoked and grants no authority.
A pinned Assurance downgrade lacks either active-key NIP-01 consent or current recovery-authority proof.
Presented Assurance hints or state conflict with a locally retained valid pin and cannot advance or downgrade it.
A rotation breadcrumb names a successor outside the accepted rotation.
A retiring profile carries a NIP-05 identifier already repointed to the successor.
A compromise-driven rotation attempts to produce a v1 breadcrumb.
The presented publishing key, subject, role, or delegation identifier does not match the active Core delegation.
An event signed by a revoked epoch key was created after revoked_at.
The verifier clock is after the delegation valid_until bound.
A KERI threshold is satisfied only if advisory vouches are counted.
A private broadcast post used the withdrawn NIP-59 wrapping path.
Relay rejected the write after NIP-42 AUTH, so the failure is permanent.
A .onion host was sent to a clearnet resolver instead of Tor.
Strict mode started with egress-over-Tor disabled without explicit user choice.
Friend-cache content was not owner-signed non-KERI content.
A Heterodyne-aware relay profile changed vanilla NIP-01 read/write behavior.
A receiver encountered an incompatible future major version.

Version-stamp policy failed because a required stamp was absent; a present stamp was duplicated, malformed, or not the exact supported non-future-major family version; or the event class forbids any stamp.
A kind:31001 NID delegation lacked the epoch-key Schnorr sig or the NID Ed25519 nid_proof.
An Ed25519 nid_proof did not verify against the advertised NID over the pinned binding payload.
A kind:31010 node advertisement was past its expiry.
A NID revoked by the KEL was used as a delegate despite the identity document still listing it.
An org member NID add carried only one of the required member-KEL and org-admin-threshold authorizations.
A Social candidate fails its canonical NIP-01 event-id or BIP-340 signature verification.
An event does not use the represented persona active key or an explicitly authorized actual signer with mandatory Comms automation attribution.
A Social replaceable candidate does not match the requested NIP-01 author, kind, and parameterized d-tag coordinate.
A kind:30078 DM invite was signed by a publishing key with no valid kind:31001 delegation to the persona.
A kind:30078 DM invite was signed by a device whose kind:31001 delegation is revoked.
The config repository RID appeared on a published surface (kind:31005, kind:31010, kind:0, NIP-65, or a NIP-51 list).
A kind:4550 approval's moderator is not listed in the kind:34550 declaration resolved as-of the approval's anchor.
An epoch-key-signed Heterodyne event required to carry kel_head does not carry exactly one well-formed instance (absent, duplicate, or malformed).
The kel_head tag's decimal seq does not equal the s value of the KEL event it names once that event is resolved on the accepted KEL.
A kel_head tag appears on an event class whose Core applicability rules forbid it (kind:31002/31003 KEL events, Marmot outer or inner events, or non-stamping rotation breadcrumbs).
A structurally valid kel_head names an event that is not on the persona's accepted KEL; the verifier flags equivocation and surfaces it through the §13 security-warning interface.
The signing epoch key is retroactively non-authoritative at the event's created_at: an accepted compromise-declaring rotation covers created_at under effective_compromise_since - 300 seconds.

Acceptance rests on relay-only key-material state (kind:31002/31003/31001); under deny-until-repo policy the event does not take effect until repo-carried, and provisional-accept results MUST NOT be reported as final.
A prior provisional or §4.5.1-accelerator acceptance is withdrawn after convergence-gated repo reconciliation, a KEL update, or later full verification contradicts it.
A repo presented a key-material head regressing below a previously finalized canonical head without an authenticated re-anchor.
KERI export failed because accepted Assurance state uses a construct with no semantics-preserving canonical-KERI mapping (UNMAPPABLE_FEATURE).
KERI export failed because a mapping exists but the target cryptographic suite is unavailable locally (UNSUPPORTED_CRYPTO_SUITE).
KERI export failed because required accepted Assurance events or attachments are unavailable (INCOMPLETE_EXPORT).
A KEL event or stream was presented in KERI10JSON/CESR on the Heterodyne wire or as storage; NIP-01 with nip01_raw is the only wire and storage format.
A derived export AID or its did:webs DID was substituted for the persona npub where the spec requires the npub; the export identity is never an alternate authoritative identity.
The claim or revocation does not satisfy its registered Comms schema.
The claim_id does not equal the lowercase SHA-256 digest of the canonical semantic body.
An issuer, subject, or proof key reference is malformed or uses an unregistered type.
The outer Nostr claim or revocation event signature is invalid.
Core/KEL validation does not establish the issuer's claimed authority at issuance time.
The claim is cryptographically valid but its issuer is outside the verifier's trust policy.
The claim issuance chain contains a repeated claim identifier.
The claim issuance chain exceeds the strict eight-edge limit.
The parent claim does not authorize the child issuer to redelegate.
A child claim widens scope, audience, resources, validity, or delegation depth.
Authorization use requires a fresh proof of possession that was not supplied.
The registered native proof profile did not validate possession of the subject key.
A persona-issued authorization is not reachable from authoritative canonical repository state.
Concurrent non-monotonic claim-ledger state remains unresolved and cannot authorize.
The claim's bounded validity interval has ended.
An irreversible valid revocation covers the claim.
The signer is not permitted to revoke this authorization or descriptive assertion.
A device lacks an active durable NID-bearing claim-ledger-reader authorization.
Presented claim-ledger state regresses below a previously finalized checkpoint.
The minting node lacks active oidc-token-issuer authority for the persona.
The minting node cannot decrypt or use an active shared issuer signing key.
The authoritative ledger checkpoint exceeds the issuer manifest's at-most-300-second freshness bound.
The requesting OAuth/OIDC client is not explicitly registered.
The request uses Client Credentials, implicit, password, or another prohibited grant.
The requested claim release lacks the required persona consent.
Requested claims exceed the intersection of scope, audience, policy, consent, trust, and active state.
Discovery metadata, JWT iss, or continuity state names a different exact issuer URL.
A JWT is missing or misuses the token-type separation required by the profile.
The JWT audience does not authorize the relying party or protected resource.
The referenced status evidence does not establish VALID: it is INVALID, stale, outside ttl, digest-mismatched, out of index bounds, or otherwise unverifiable.
A role-addressed delegation does not use the exact registered namespace and role identifier syntax.
The registered role-key proof is missing, malformed, or invalid over the profile binding.
A universal-launcher fragment is unknown, malformed, oversized, or contains an invalid NIP-19 entity.
A public-reader bootstrap hint violates the normalized relay URL or local-network exclusion rules.
Public-reader mode was asked to render Tier 2 plaintext or interpret Tier 3 ciphertext as public content.
The agent workload registration is malformed, incompatible, non-final, or grants unbounded automated publication.

The workload access token is not usable: it fails signature, type, issuer, client, identity, audience, scope, role, ledger, status, lifetime, or structural validation. The specific condition is recorded only in the encrypted audit.
The per-use workload JWK proof is missing, replayed, malformed, or mismatched with cnf.jkt.
The token, registration, selected signing key, key class, optional association kind/value, or event pubkey disagrees with current authorization.
An automated publication selected the persona key without the exact explicit OIDC persona-signing scope.
An agent-authored event has missing, malformed, reordered, or identity-mismatched canonical attribution.
The requested authored event kind has no active revision-3 agent-attribution profile.
A one-time invitation or response was processed at or after its signed expiry.
Local ordinary-conversation policy explicitly rejects an otherwise valid Marmot Welcome.
A one-time invitation was presented or redeemed for a purpose other than its exact signed purpose.
A one-time invite descriptor signature, NIP-59 responder binding, secret proof, or capability binding is invalid.
A different authenticated account or canonical response already reserved the one-time invitation.
A preauthorized Control invite exceeds its exact bound signer-grant template, persona, client, signer, method, kind, limit, or prompt-free policy.
A full node accepts no new enrollment for this request. Disabled policy, exhausted capacity, and expired enrollment state are indistinguishable to the requester.
Finite Welcome-processing or KeyPackage-replenishment rate or burst capacity is exhausted.
The node cannot replenish the public Control KeyPackage pool while its global pending-enrollment cap is full.
A Device Authorization user code is not usable, whether malformed, unknown, or atomically invalidated after five failed guesses.
A Device Authorization guess or poll violates per-code, node-wide, interval, or slow-down limits.
The approving and initiating displays do not show the identical user code and client fingerprint.
The authenticated private authorization view is conflicted, older than 300 seconds, or not freshly synchronized for mutation.
The selected Control KeyPackage is malformed, expired, unsupported, or does not belong to the advertised full-node account.
The Control group is enrollment-only and the requested method requires an active exact signer grant.
The inner Control application event or canonical frame violates its closed kind, tag, version, profile, member, or payload rules.
The private server-side signer grant is missing, stale beyond policy, unauthorized, forked, revoked, or contains a conflicting expansion.

The Control access token is not usable: it fails type, signature, issuer, time, client, exact audience, sender constraint, grant, scope, private-state checkpoint, or structural validation. The specific condition is recorded only in the encrypted audit.
A Control client requested or presented a refresh token even though the profile requires fresh node-local issuance.
A logical operation identifier was reused for a different method, object, or canonical payload.
A prior node may have committed the mutation, but no authoritative result proves whether repeating it is safe.
The authenticated Control request expired before reservation or execution.
A request identifier was reused with different canonical bound bytes in the same persona vault.
An automated principal requested a method outside its closed agentic Control surface.
An automated principal requested private key material or raw signing authority.
An automated principal attempted to bypass its selected persona vault, signing key, or key class.
An automated principal attempted to omit, alter, or falsify canonical agent attribution.
The requested method, event kind, value, destination, or object is outside the exact active signer grant.
The attributed unsigned event exceeds the exact grant's finite event-byte ceiling.
The publication intent exceeds the exact grant's finite request window or request-count limit.
Evidence indicates an automated publication omitted mandatory agent attribution.
Evidence indicates an automated publication falsified mandatory agent attribution.
Evidence indicates an automated principal bypassed the required token and intent-level publication path.
An agent-policy receipt is malformed, unverifiable, secret-bearing, or does not bind exactly one actual event author, verified agent association, policy version, decision, and evidence set.
A policy-list entry does not bind the same actual event author, receipt identifier, and reason code.
A Heterodyne-private group has no currently authorized Radicle route and cannot use a public fallback.
No trusted-seed ACL projection is available for the requested private route.
A trusted-seed ACL is malformed, future-issued, incorrectly signed, or otherwise invalid.
The selected trusted-seed ACL has reached its signed expiry.
The selected trusted-seed ACL is not newer than accepted state or names an older Marmot group transition.
More than one distinct valid trusted-seed ACL claims the same greatest sequence.
Trusted-seed ACL state has no unique predecessor-linked head, seed grant, account entry, or writer ref.
The authenticated account, seed NID, operation, or target writer ref is outside the current ACL.
The requested seed NID is explicitly revoked by the current ACL projection.
Private relay admission lacks successful NIP-42 authentication by the account being authorized.
The request and ACL disagree on h, private RID, current Marmot transition, or the selected seed route.
A trusted-seed write does not carry one complete signed kind-445 Nostr event with a valid identifier and BIP-340 signature.
Private relay admission metadata contains a missing, malformed, alternate, or additional request member.
A private relay request capability or its authenticated consume binding was already used.
A routing binding has the wrong administrator, canonical Marmot routing commit, h value, or repository genesis digest.
Different otherwise valid routing bindings claim the same canonical Marmot h.
A writer or relay ref is not authorized to contribute objects to the routing-generation union.
A publisher or relay acknowledged a Marmot object before the required exact-byte durability boundary.
A sender NID is not authorized to contribute a contact bundle to the private persona repository.
A persona-inbox bootstrap attempts to consume a Marmot KeyPackage already consumed by another accepted or quarantined bundle.
An automated Marmot operation requests a group, application kind, media type, size, rate, or burst outside its workload token.
A Tier 3 audience-key recipient is not an active delegated human-device publishing key in the effective audience.
Relay state was presented as canonical profile state without repository selection.
The claimed vanilla profile publisher is not the one active delegated profile-publisher key.
Optional NIP-05 resolution did not return the designated profile publisher key.
Retired-key content claims a created_at outside that key's authority window.
Retired-key content falls at or after the accepted compromise_since cutoff.
A newly accepted node advertisement is more than 300 seconds from verifier time.
Known verifier clock uncertainty exceeds the 300-second acceptance window.
A node advertisement expiry is not strictly after created_at.
A node advertisement lifetime exceeds 86400 seconds.
A Workspace object or its canonical encoding does not match its closed schema.
A Workspace active-key signature or its exact policy, predecessor, checkpoint, or repository binding is invalid.
The configured trusted repository verification boundary did not authenticate one complete exact current Workspace repository view.
Required authority heads or role paths conflict or are incomparable.
Inheritance, a grant, or delegation attempts to widen an applicable ceiling.
Current effective Workspace policy denies the operation.
The configured resolver handle is not the latest accepted generation, is superseded, not yet observed, expired, or exceeds its maximum age.
A bilateral source affiliation exceeds its proof and grace bounds.
The target or requesting device is not currently authorized.
A requested historical key falls outside the active grant history mode.
An authorized responder has no resource matching the requested identifier.
The responder is not an authorized key custodian for the resource and checkpoint.
A public projection correlates a concealed workspace, role, relationship, repository, or resource.
A Workspace nonce, approval, relationship, grant, or key envelope was replayed.
A request does not resolve exactly one vault for its exact active persona key.
The exact selected signer and key class are unavailable in the selected persona vault; no fallback is attempted.
A presented or requested signer binding differs from the authoritative server-side grant.
The selected signer grant is not yet issued, expired, revoked, or otherwise inactive.
NIP-46 client metadata or requested permissions exceed the exact server-side methods, kinds, audience, or limits.
Persona-key signing lacks an explicit grant authorized by the active persona account.
A pending OIDC authorization cannot activate the presented NIP-46 connection secret.
A consumed one-use NIP-46 connection secret was presented again.
An automated publication cannot receive a signature because valid Comms automation attribution was not produced first.
A compromise completion omits or changes a required grant, client, delegate, node, agent, seed, Marmot leaf, group transition, or fresh KeyPackage action.
A continuing subordinate authority lacks a fresh explicit post-compromise authorization.
The authoritative signer grant, request limits, or usage record is structurally invalid.
A signer grant fails its domain-separated BIP-340 authorization signature.
The presented signer grant is not the unique authenticated predecessor/revocation head.
The authoritative per-grant usage record has exhausted its finite request window.
The authoritative per-grant usage state does not prove that the exact request ID and canonical digest were durably reserved before signing.
The signer invocation was attempted without authoritative persisted executing state and its grant-bound idempotency token.
The presented NIP-46 request has an invalid bounded wire ID or its sign_event parameter is not one unambiguous closed standard EventTemplate.
Authoritative usage or replay state is not bound to the collision-resistant digest and complete authority tuple of the authenticated current grant.
An executing signing operation produced an invalid, failed, timed-out, or otherwise uncertain signer effect and requires a durable non-reusable indeterminate transition.
A NIP-46 activation differs from its exact approved OIDC, grant, persona, client, audience, signer, or key-class binding.
Caller attribution hints differ from the authenticated workload policy bound by the signer grant.
An automated publication intent violates its single closed unsigned-intent contract.
The signer returned altered event fields or an invalid canonical NIP-01 event ID or BIP-340 signature.
A reset grant or completion lacks its required domain-separated BIP-340 authority signature or pinned Assurance binding.
The signed reset grant does not exactly bind the authoritative pre-reset persona-vault inventory and revision.
Reset completion evidence is not authoritative, exact, fresh, consecutive, successor-bound, or cryptographically transition-complete.
